# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

def _cost_cell(pricing, facts, trial, tin, tout, model_override):
    """USD for one trial row; None renders n/a (unpriced/unknown model)."""
    model = (facts.get(trial) or {}).get("model") or model_override
    entry = fa_usage.price_entry(pricing, model) if model else None
    if entry is None:
        return None
    return fa_usage.cost_usd(entry, tin or 0, tout or 0)


def render(runs_dir: Path, expected=None, model_override=None):
    """Build the summary (lines, problems) for a runs dir — pure, testable."""
    runs_dir = Path(runs_dir)
    paths = sorted(glob.glob(str(runs_dir / "*" / "results.json")))
    lines = ["### fa on terminal-bench", ""]
    problems = []

    if not paths:
        lines.append("**No results.json produced — the tb run did not complete.**")
        problems.append("no results.json produced")
        return lines, problems

    pricing = fa_usage.load_pricing(_PRICING_PATH)
    facts = _session_facts(runs_dir)
    rows = []
    for p in paths:
        data = json.loads(Path(p).read_text())
        for r in data.get("results", []):
            resolved = r.get("is_resolved")
            mark = {True: "yes", False: "no", None: "pending"}[resolved]
            tin = r.get("total_input_tokens")
            tout = r.get("total_output_tokens")
            cost = _cost_cell(
                pricing, facts, r.get("trial_name", "?"), tin, tout, model_override
            )
            rows.append((
                r.get("task_id", "?"), r.get("trial_name", "?"), mark,
                r.get("failure_mode") or "", tin, tout, cost,
            ))
    n_resolved = sum(1 for r in rows if r[2] == "yes")
    accuracy = n_resolved / len(rows) if rows else 0.0
    missing = expected - len(rows) if expected is not None else 0
    note = (
        f" — {expected - len(rows)} of {expected} expected tasks missing"
        " (shard lost or timed out)" if expected is not None and len(rows) < expected else ""
    )
    lines.append(
        f"**{n_resolved}/{len(rows)} resolved — accuracy {accuracy:.0%}{note}**"
    )

    # Failure families (issue #142): the re-run delta is reported per
    # cluster, not just as one accuracy number. `unset` covers both
    # resolved trials (tb's default mode) and unresolved ones whose
    # tests ran and failed — the model side.
    #
    # gh-1308 (NG2/AC3): agent_timeout rows split by recorded tokens —
    # a 0-token timeout is a provider hang (the endpoint accepted the
    # request and streamed nothing), not a trial that ran out of clock
    # doing real work. The explicit count is the provider-health
    # regression guard across bench runs.
    modes = {}
    hang = work = 0
    for _, _, mark, mode, tin, tout, _ in rows:
        key = mode or "unset"
        if key == "agent_timeout":
            if not tin and not tout:
                key = "agent_timeout (0 tokens — provider hang)"
                hang += 1
            else:
                key = "agent_timeout (real work, cap exhausted)"
                work += 1
        modes[(key, mark)] = modes.get((key, mark), 0) + 1
    lines.append("Failure families (mode x resolved):")
    for (mode, mark), n in sorted(modes.items()):
        lines.append(f"- {mode or 'unset'} / {mark}: {n}")
    if hang or work:
        lines.append(
            f"**zero-token timeouts (provider hang): {hang}**"
            f" — agent_timeout split: {hang} with 0 tokens (provider hang),"
            f" {work} with real work (cap exhausted)"
        )
    lines.append("")

    # Token/cost totals (issue #1123): sums over exactly the rows above.
    total_in = sum(r[4] or 0 for r in rows)
    total_out = sum(r[5] or 0 for r in rows)
    priced = [r[6] for r in rows if r[6] is not None]
    # Same unpriced rule as the harbor summary: only rows that recorded
    # tokens but carry no price count. Zero-token rows render n/a but are
    # not unpriced spend.
    unpriced = sum(1 for r in rows if (r[4] or r[5]) and r[6] is None)
    if any(r[4] or r[5] for r in rows):
        cost_total = f"${sum(priced):.4f}" if priced else "n/a"
        suffix = f" — {unpriced} trial(s) unpriced (model missing from pricing.json)" if unpriced else ""
        lines.append(f"**tokens in/out: {total_in}/{total_out} — est. cost: {cost_total}{suffix}**")
        estimated = sum((facts.get(r[1]) or {}).get("estimated", 0) for r in rows)
        if estimated:
            lines.append(
                f"includes ~{estimated} estimated tokens (chars/4 where the provider omitted usage)"
            )
    lines.append("| task | trial | resolved | failure mode | tokens in/out | est cost |")
    lines.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for task, trial, mark, mode, tin, tout, cost in rows:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1311
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1311
- **Title**: gh-1308 [BUG] bench: GLM zero-byte hangs burn the whole agent cap — 11/59 trials died at 0 tokens (watchdog replays, cap clock keeps ticking, no fallback take-over)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1308` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +965
- **Deletions**: -334
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T09:11:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T12:13:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #1308
### Root Cause

- A GLM/zai endpoint that accepts requests but streams nothing was killed only by the agent's one-shot run-idle watchdog; the transient-retry ladder replayed the watchdog-cancelled request, but the watchdog timer was never re-armed — the replay ran unbounded until the trial cap, recording `agent_timeout` with 0 tokens (run 37418229569: 11/59 trials).
- The zero-byte replay class also never engaged the model-roles fallback chain: its verdict matched no transport pattern, so a hung primary was never handed off to the next configured model.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`: after 2 consecutive pre-commit attempts killed by the run-idle watchdog with zero output, the ladder stops replaying and fails the call with a retryable `zero-byte stall` terminal (`zeroByteStallTag`, `maxZeroByteWatchdogAttempts = 2`) instead of spending the remaining budget — verdict lands at ≈ 2×watchdog-interval, not the cap. Other failure classes keep the full 3-attempt budget.
- `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`: the run-idle watchdog re-arms after each fire while the run is active, so every replayed silent attempt is bounded by the same interval (a user abort that won the race is never revived).
- `lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart` + `providers_queue_runtime.dart`: the zero-byte verdict classifies as an immediate advance — the wedged primary is skipped, the next chain entry takes over (the 429 take-over path), no same-entry paid retries (each would cost another watchdog interval).
- `bench/terminal_bench/summary.py`: `agent_timeout` rows split into `agent_timeout (0 tokens — provider hang)` vs `agent_timeout (real work, cap exhausted)`, with an explicit `zero-token timeouts (provider hang): N` count (NG2).

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/transient_retry_stream_test.dart`: synthetic silent fixture — watchdog fires → bounded replays (2, was 3) → error verdict carrying the zero-byte classification, transport-classified (NG1/AC1).
- `test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_test.dart`: real-clock end-to-end — both silent attempts watchdog-killed, run ends as a retryable error at ≈ 2×interval, well under a minutes-long cap (AC1).
- `test/model_roles/fallback_stream_test.dart`: primary zero-byte stall → `modelFallback` notice → secondary answers, its model recorded (AC2); queue classifier: zero-byte verdict → timeout death, immediate.
- `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary.py` (new): the NG2 split and explicit count; non-timeout rows render unchanged.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — 9140 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures; bench python suites (terminal_bench + harbor_fa, 54 tests) green.

### Notes

- The generic 3-attempt transient budget, the connect-stall retry leg, and every non-watchdog failure class are byte-identical — only the zero-byte watchdog class is bounded.
- A sole (no-fallback) chain now fails truthfully after the zero-byte budget instead of hanging to the cap; users can raise `agent.runIdleTimeout` / `providerTimeouts:` for legitimately slow reasoning endpoints.

# gh-1308: [BUG] bench: GLM zero-byte hangs burn the whole agent cap — 11/59 trials died at 0 tokens (watchdog replays, cap clock keeps ticking, no fallback take-over)

## Description

**Evidence** (TBench full-dataset run [37418229569](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37418229569), 2026-10-06, glm-5.3-flash, 8 shards): 11 of the first 59 scored trials died as `agent_timeout` with **0 input / 0 output tokens** — while `unset`-failures in the same run recorded real usage (2–18k tokens), so accounting works and these trials genuinely never received a single token.

Root mechanism (from trial `polyglot-c-py` agent.log, cap 1020s):

```
fa -p 'Write me a single file in /app/main.c.py ...'
note: provider zai (zai) from FA_PROVIDER_* env
… reasoning 60s
… reasoning 120s
… (nothing but "reasoning" for 480s)
[net] connection lost (run-idle watchdog replay of zero-byte request: Request was aborted) — retrying in 5s (attempt 2/3)
… reasoning 540s … 1020s  → agent_timeout, 0 tokens
```

The GLM endpoint accepts the request and streams **zero bytes for 8+ minutes**; the run-idle watchdog correctly detects and replays (attempt 2/3), the replay ALSO returns zero bytes, and the cap clock keeps burning through every retry — trial dies having never started. 11 timeout trials, spread across shards (2/1/2/0/1/2 — not one bad runner): blind-maze-explorer-algorithm (2100s cap), git-multibranch, gpt2-codegolf, path-tracing, play-zork, polyglot-c-py, polyglot-rust-c, raman-fitting.easy, chess-best-move, write-compressor, sanitize-git-repo.hard. (play-zork/git-multibranch additionally show the stuck-call watchdog — secondary pattern: endless foreground commands; the zero-byte hang is the primary one.)

**Interpretation:** provider-side hang (zai/glm under 8-shard concurrency or on hard prompts with thinking), amplified by harness retry semantics: zero-byte replays restart reasoning from zero while the trial cap keeps ticking, and no fallback model is engaged (the 429 mid-turn take-over exists; zero-byte stall does not trigger it).

**Fix directions (choose per design):**
1. Zero-byte replays consume a bounded provider-time budget: after N (e.g. 2) consecutive zero-byte replays, the turn FAILS as a retryable error instead of burning the remaining cap — the trial dies fast and truthfully (error, not timeout).
2. Watchdog zero-byte stall triggers the model-roles fallback chain (same as 429 take-over) — a hung primary hands off to the next configured model instead of replaying into the same wedged endpoint.
3. Bench observability: the run summary should separate `agent_timeout (0 tokens — provider hang)` from `agent_timeout (real work, cap exhausted)` — today they are indistinguishable without opening logs.

**Owner questions, answered in the design (2026-10-06):**
- *«Isn't there already a zero-stream timeout+retry?»* — YES: the stream idle watchdog (providerStreamIdleTimeout, 5 min) fired exactly as coded (the `attempt 2/3` replay in the log). The defect is the ARITHMETIC: 5-min idle window × up to 3 attempts > the 17-min task cap — the trial burns out without producing a token. The fix is bounding, not adding, the timeout.
- *«Reduce bench concurrency?»* — an option with a real cost (8→4 shards doubles wall time ~2h→4h). Cheaper first moves, in order: (a) bench-specific short idle timeout via the existing `providerTimeouts:` config seam (60–90s — fail-fast, 5+ attempts fit inside the same cap), (b) fallback take-over on zero-byte stall, (c) only if timeouts persist after (a)+(b) — cut shard concurrency or stagger shard starts. The shard-spread of the hangs (2/1/2/0/1/2, no start-peak concentration) does NOT prove subscription saturation, so concurrency is the last lever, not the first.

**Deeper log evidence (owner's race-condition question, 2026-10-06):** the hang is NOT only a cold-start. `chess-best-move` shows a WORKING agent (a `read` tool call answered with FileError) whose NEXT provider request then hangs zero-byte. Same spinner-only shape in `gpt2-codegolf`. Pattern: mid-conversation requests hang, not just the first one.

**Race-condition hypothesis to investigate (likely prime suspect):** the shared keep-alive provider HTTP client (sharedProviderHttpClient) reuses pooled connections; in bench containers (docker → NAT → internet), conntrack/NAT silently drops idle TCP, leaving HALF-OPEN sockets: a retry or a follow-up request written into a half-open pooled connection is accepted locally and never answered — zero bytes forever, until the 5-min idle watchdog aborts. It fits every observation: hangs mid-conversation (pool reuse after tool-call gaps), retries hanging identically (retry may pick the SAME poisoned pool entry), spread across shards (per-container NAT state), zero tokens.
**Consequences for the fix:**
- A watchdog replay MUST dial a FRESH connection (evict the pool entry / bypass keep-alive for the retry), not reuse the socket that just delivered zero bytes.
- Cheap validation: TCP keepalive or a shorter idle floor on the bench profile (providerTimeouts) would surface half-opens sooner; if hang count collapses with keep-alive DISABLED in a test bench run, the hypothesis is confirmed.
- Add to AC1: a fixture where the server accepts the socket and never replies must show the retry arriving on a NEW connection (assert connection reuse-off for watchdog replays).

**Field evidence — this hits INTERACTIVE users, not just bench (2026-10-06, second developer's report via owner):** in the fa TUI the same zero-byte hang shows as: you send a message, the agent «thinks», you come back an HOUR later to «agent stalled» with zero output — one overnight session sat «agent staled for 570 minutes». The session is effectively lost («сессия в сраку идёт»). The omp tool on the same machine/provider has NEVER done this to him («с тех пор ни одной такой проблемы»). So the class is user-facing and retention-critical, not a bench corner case.

**What this adds to the fix:**
- The TUI stall detector («agent stalled» notice) REPORTS but does not RECOVER — the turn hangs forever unless the user babysits. The bounded-replay + fallback fix must apply to the interactive path exactly as to bench: a wedged zero-byte request must surface as a retried/failed-over TURN, never a silent stall.
- AC addition: **AC4 — interactive recovery**: with the synthetic zero-byte fixture, a TUI session shows the retry/fallback happening in-band (and the turn completing or failing with a named error within the bounded budget) — «stalled for N minutes» as a terminal state is eliminated.
- Severity note for triage: user quote — he switched back to omp because of this; treat as P1.

## NEVER-AGAIN

- **NG1**: a synthetic provider fixture that accepts and streams nothing must produce: watchdog fires → bounded replays → error verdict with the zero-byte classification — covered by a unit test at the stream/watchdog layer (provider_common.dart).
- **NG2**: bench aggregate reports the zero-token-timeout count explicitly (regression guard for provider health across bench runs).

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: replay-into-hang no longer burns the whole cap: measured on the synthetic fixture, verdict time ≈ N×watchdog-interval, not the full agent cap.
- AC2: fallback take-over on zero-byte stall proven in a test (primary hangs, secondary answers, turn completes with the fallback's model recorded).
- AC3: bench summary split lands (NG2); the next full-dataset run shows the classification without log diving.

Assigning ai-teammate per owner directive for this flow. Refs: #1122 (cap ladder), #1185 (liveness watchdog family), provider watchdogs in provider_common.dart; run 37418229569 artifacts tb-runs-shard-* (agent.log per trial).

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gh-1308 NG2/AC3: the run summary separates zero-token provider hangs
+from real cap-exhausted timeouts, and reports the zero-token-timeout
+count explicitly — a regression guard for provider health across bench
+runs (today an `agent_timeout` row is indistinguishable from a trial
+that did real work until someone opens the agent logs).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
+"""
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
+    "summary_legacy", Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "summary.py"
+)
+summary = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+sys.modules["summary_legacy"] = summary
+spec.loader.exec_module(summary)
+
+
+def trial(task, name, resolved, mode, tin, tout):
+    return {
+        "task_id": task,
+        "trial_name": name,
+        "is_resolved": resolved,
+        "failure_mode": mode,
+        "total_input_tokens": tin,
+        "total_output_tokens": tout,
+    }
+
+
+class ZeroTokenTimeoutSplitTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.runs = Path(self.tmp.name)
+        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
+
+    def write_run(self, results):
+        run = self.runs / "shard-1"
+        run.mkdir(parents=True)
+        (run / "results.json").write_text(json.dumps({"results": results}))
+
+    def test_ng2_zero_token_timeouts_counted_explicitly(self):
+        # The gh-1308 evidence shape: agent_timeout rows with 0 tokens
+        # (provider hang) next to one that burned real tokens before the
+        # cap, other failure modes untouched.
+        self.write_run([
+            trial("t1", "x.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "agent_timeout", 0, 0),
+            trial("t2", "y.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "agent_timeout", None, None),
+            trial("t3", "z.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "agent_timeout", 4200, 900),
+            trial("t4", "w.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "tests_failed", 800, 200),
+            trial("t5", "v.1-of-1.shard-1", True, None, 120, 40),
+        ])
+        lines, problems = summary.render(self.runs)
+        out = "\n".join(lines)
+        self.assertEqual(problems, [])
+        # NG2: the explicit count — the provider-health regression guard.
+        self.assertIn("zero-token timeouts (provider hang): 2", out)
+        self.assertIn("1 with real work (cap exhausted)", out)
+        # AC3: the failure families carry the split, so the classification
+        # is visible without log diving.
+        self.assertIn("agent_timeout (0 tokens — provider hang) / no: 2", out)
+        self.assertIn("agent_timeout (real work, cap exhausted) / no: 1", out)
+        # A flat `agent_timeout` family row must NOT survive the split.
+        self.assertNotIn("- agent_timeout /", out)
+
+    def test_no_agent_timeout_rows_no_split_line(self):
+        self.write_run([
+            trial("t1", "x.1-of-1.shard-1", True, None, 10, 5),
+            trial("t2", "y.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "tests_failed", 0, 0),
+        ])
+        lines, _ = summary.render(self.runs)
+        out = "\n".join(lines)
+        self.assertNotIn("zero-token timeouts", out)
+        self.assertNotIn("provider hang", out)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one

Wait — important: in `classifyQueueDeath`, the zero-byte check is placed AFTER the `retryClass != null → QueueDeathKind.finishReason` check. Let me trace the zero-byte terminal through `classifyQueueDeath`:

The zero-byte terminal message: 'Provider zero-byte stall after 2 attempt(s) over 962s — ... ($zeroByteStallTag). Attempts: ... The failure is retryable: ...'

1. `isBudgetExhaustion` — no.
2. `finishReasonRetryClass(event.error)` — is this null for the zero-byte terminal? `finishReasonRetryClass` presumably parses the wire finish_reason from `rawStopReason` or vendor words. The zero-byte message has no rawStopReason (constructed fresh with none). Let me check `finishReasonRetryClass` to be sure it doesn't classify based on errorMessage text. If it returns non-null for something in the message (e.g. "retryable"?), the queue death would be `finishReason` (non-immediate) BEFORE reaching the zero-byte check. The queue test asserts timeout/immediate for the full terminal wording — and CI is green per ticket, so `finishReasonRetryClass` returns null here. Good — and the test pins it.

3. Zero-byte check → timeout+immediate. Good.

Now the roles ladder `_nonQueueRetryable` ordering: budget → zero-byte → rate-limit → transport. Wait — should zero-byte also be checked BEFORE budget? A zero-byte message can't contain budget words. Fine.

One more check in the roles ladder: `_transportPatterns` gained the zero-byte tag regex. Where is `_transportPatterns` used? `isTransientTransportError(event.error)`. Since the zero-byte branch returns earlier with immediate, the pattern addition matters for OTHER layers: `classifyQueueDeath`'s `_labeledDeath` fallback (`isTransientTransportError(error)`) — but the explicit tag check precedes it. And the zero-byte tag in `_transientNetworkPatterns` (providers file) makes `isTransientNetworkError` classify it retryable — matters for a re-entered ladder (failover target builds a fresh ladder, and if the SECONDARY also stalls... the secondary's own attempts are fresh; the tag only appears in the terminal). Actually there's a subtle reason: `_replaysAttempt`/`_retryableWireFailure` on a re-entered ladder... the terminal is pushed out of the ladder, not re-entered. def _cost_cell(pricing, facts, trial, tin, tout, model_override):
    """USD for one trial row; None renders n/a (unpriced/unknown model)."""
    model = (facts.get(trial) or {}).get("model") or model_override
    entry = fa_usage.price_entry(pricing, model) if model else None
    if entry is None:
        return None
    return fa_usage.cost_usd(entry, tin or 0, tout or 0)


def render(runs_dir: Path, expected=None, model_override=None):
    """Build the summary (lines, problems) for a runs dir — pure, testable."""
    runs_dir = Path(runs_dir)
    paths = sorted(glob.glob(str(runs_dir / "*" / "results.json")))
    lines = ["### fa on terminal-bench", ""]
    problems = []

    if not paths:
        lines.append("**No results.json produced — the tb run did not complete.**")
        problems.append("no results.json produced")
        return lines, problems

    pricing = fa_usage.load_pricing(_PRICING_PATH)
    facts = _session_facts(runs_dir)
    rows = []
    for p in paths:
        data = json.loads(Path(p).read_text())
        for r in data.get("results", []):
            resolved = r.get("is_resolved")
            mark = {True: "yes", False: "no", None: "pending"}[resolved]
            tin = r.get("total_input_tokens")
            tout = r.get("total_output_tokens")
            cost = _cost_cell(
                pricing, facts, r.get("trial_name", "?"), tin, tout, model_override
            )
            rows.append((
                r.get("task_id", "?"), r.get("trial_name", "?"), mark,
                r.get("failure_mode") or "", tin, tout, cost,
            ))
    n_resolved = sum(1 for r in rows if r[2] == "yes")
    accuracy = n_resolved / len(rows) if rows else 0.0
    missing = expected - len(rows) if expected is not None else 0
    note = (
        f" — {expected - len(rows)} of {expected} expected tasks missing"
        " (shard lost or timed out)" if expected is not None and len(rows) < expected else ""
    )
    lines.append(
        f"**{n_resolved}/{len(rows)} resolved — accuracy {accuracy:.0%}{note}**"
    )

    # Failure families (issue #142): the re-run delta is reported per
    # cluster, not just as one accuracy number. `unset` covers both
    # resolved trials (tb's default mode) and unresolved ones whose
    # tests ran and failed — the model side.
    #
    # gh-1308 (NG2/AC3): agent_timeout rows split by recorded tokens —
    # a 0-token timeout is a provider hang (the endpoint accepted the
    # request and streamed nothing), not a trial that ran out of clock
    # doing real work. The explicit count is the provider-health
    # regression guard across bench runs.
    modes = {}
    hang = work = 0
    for _, _, mark, mode, tin, tout, _ in rows:
        key = mode or "unset"
        if key == "agent_timeout":
            if not tin and not tout:
                key = "agent_timeout (0 tokens — provider hang)"
                hang += 1
            else:
                key = "agent_timeout (real work, cap exhausted)"
                work += 1
        modes[(key, mark)] = modes.get((key, mark), 0) + 1
    lines.append("Failure families (mode x resolved):")
    for (mode, mark), n in sorted(modes.items()):
        lines.append(f"- {mode or 'unset'} / {mark}: {n}")
    if hang or work:
        lines.append(
            f"**zero-token timeouts (provider hang): {hang}**"
            f" — agent_timeout split: {hang} with 0 tokens (provider hang),"
            f" {work} with real work (cap exhausted)"
        )
    lines.append("")

    # Token/cost totals (issue #1123): sums over exactly the rows above.
    total_in = sum(r[4] or 0 for r in rows)
    total_out = sum(r[5] or 0 for r in rows)
    priced = [r[6] for r in rows if r[6] is not None]
    # Same unpriced rule as the harbor summary: only rows that recorded
    # tokens but carry no price count. Zero-token rows render n/a but are
    # not unpriced spend.
    unpriced = sum(1 for r in rows if (r[4] or r[5]) and r[6] is None)
    if any(r[4] or r[5] for r in rows):
        cost_total = f"${sum(priced):.4f}" if priced else "n/a"
        suffix = f" — {unpriced} trial(s) unpriced (model missing from pricing.json)" if unpriced else ""
        lines.append(f"**tokens in/out: {total_in}/{total_out} — est. cost: {cost_total}{suffix}**")
        estimated = sum((facts.get(r[1]) or {}).get("estimated", 0) for r in rows)
        if estimated:

                f"includes ~{estimated} estimated tokens (chars/4 where the provider omitted usage)"
            )
    lines.append("| task | trial | resolved | failure mode | tokens in/out | est cost |")

    for task, trial, mark, mode, tin, tout, cost in rows:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1311
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1311
- **Title**: gh-1308 [BUG] bench: GLM zero-byte hangs burn the whole agent cap — 11/59 trials died at 0 tokens (watchdog replays, cap clock keeps ticking, no fallback take-over)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1308` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +965
- **Deletions**: -334
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T09:11:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T12:13:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #1308
### Root Cause

- A GLM/zai endpoint that accepts requests but streams nothing was killed only by the agent's one-shot run-idle watchdog; the transient-retry ladder replayed the watchdog-cancelled request, but the watchdog timer was never re-armed — the replay ran unbounded until the trial cap, recording `agent_timeout` with 0 tokens (run 37418229569: 11/59 trials).
- The zero-byte replay class also never engaged the model-roles fallback chain: its verdict matched no transport pattern, so a hung primary was never handed off to the next configured model.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`: after 2 consecutive pre-commit attempts killed by the run-idle watchdog with zero output, the ladder stops replaying and fails the call with a retryable `zero-byte stall` terminal (`zeroByteStallTag`, `maxZeroByteWatchdogAttempts = 2`) instead of spending the remaining budget — verdict lands at ≈ 2×watchdog-interval, not the cap. Other failure classes keep the full 3-attempt budget.
- `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`: the run-idle watchdog re-arms after each fire while the run is active, so every replayed silent attempt is bounded by the same interval (a user abort that won the race is never revived).
- `lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart` + `providers_queue_runtime.dart`: the zero-byte verdict classifies as an immediate advance — the wedged primary is skipped, the next chain entry takes over (the 429 take-over path), no same-entry paid retries (each would cost another watchdog interval).
- `bench/terminal_bench/summary.py`: `agent_timeout` rows split into `agent_timeout (0 tokens — provider hang)` vs `agent_timeout (real work, cap exhausted)`, with an explicit `zero-token timeouts (provider hang): N` count (NG2).

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/transient_retry_stream_test.dart`: synthetic silent fixture — watchdog fires → bounded replays (2, was 3) → error verdict carrying the zero-byte classification, transport-classified (NG1/AC1).
- `test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_test.dart`: real-clock end-to-end — both silent attempts watchdog-killed, run ends as a retryable error at ≈ 2×interval, well under a minutes-long cap (AC1).
- `test/model_roles/fallback_stream_test.dart`: primary zero-byte stall → `modelFallback` notice → secondary answers, its model recorded (AC2); queue classifier: zero-byte verdict → timeout death, immediate.
- `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary.py` (new): the NG2 split and explicit count; non-timeout rows render unchanged.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — 9140 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures; bench python suites (terminal_bench + harbor_fa, 54 tests) green.

### Notes

- The generic 3-attempt transient budget, the connect-stall retry leg, and every non-watchdog failure class are byte-identical — only the zero-byte watchdog class is bounded.
- A sole (no-fallback) chain now fails truthfully after the zero-byte budget instead of hanging to the cap; users can raise `agent.runIdleTimeout` / `providerTimeouts:` for legitimately slow reasoning endpoints.

# gh-1308: [BUG] bench: GLM zero-byte hangs burn the whole agent cap — 11/59 trials died at 0 tokens (watchdog replays, cap clock keeps ticking, no fallback take-over)

## Description

**Evidence** (TBench full-dataset run [37418229569](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37418229569), 2026-10-06, glm-5.3-flash, 8 shards): 11 of the first 59 scored trials died as `agent_timeout` with **0 input / 0 output tokens** — while `unset`-failures in the same run recorded real usage (2–18k tokens), so accounting works and these trials genuinely never received a single token.

Root mechanism (from trial `polyglot-c-py` agent.log, cap 1020s):

```
fa -p 'Write me a single file in /app/main.c.py ...'
note: provider zai (zai) from FA_PROVIDER_* env
… reasoning 60s
… reasoning 120s
… (nothing but "reasoning" for 480s)
[net] connection lost (run-idle watchdog replay of zero-byte request: Request was aborted) — retrying in 5s (attempt 2/3)
… reasoning 540s … 1020s  → agent_timeout, 0 tokens
```

The GLM endpoint accepts the request and streams **zero bytes for 8+ minutes**; the run-idle watchdog correctly detects and replays (attempt 2/3), the replay ALSO returns zero bytes, and the cap clock keeps burning through every retry — trial dies having never started. 11 timeout trials, spread across shards (2/1/2/0/1/2 — not one bad runner): blind-maze-explorer-algorithm (2100s cap), git-multibranch, gpt2-codegolf, path-tracing, play-zork, polyglot-c-py, polyglot-rust-c, raman-fitting.easy, chess-best-move, write-compressor, sanitize-git-repo.hard. (play-zork/git-multibranch additionally show the stuck-call watchdog — secondary pattern: endless foreground commands; the zero-byte hang is the primary one.)

**Interpretation:** provider-side hang (zai/glm under 8-shard concurrency or on hard prompts with thinking), amplified by harness retry semantics: zero-byte replays restart reasoning from zero while the trial cap keeps ticking, and no fallback model is engaged (the 429 mid-turn take-over exists; zero-byte stall does not trigger it).

**Fix directions (choose per design):**
1. Zero-byte replays consume a bounded provider-time budget: after N (e.g. 2) consecutive zero-byte replays, the turn FAILS as a retryable error instead of burning the remaining cap — the trial dies fast and truthfully (error, not timeout).
2. Watchdog zero-byte stall triggers the model-roles fallback chain (same as 429 take-over) — a hung primary hands off to the next configured model instead of replaying into the same wedged endpoint.
3. Bench observability: the run summary should separate `agent_timeout (0 tokens — provider hang)` from `agent_timeout (real work, cap exhausted)` — today they are indistinguishable without opening logs.

**Owner questions, answered in the design (2026-10-06):**
- *«Isn't there already a zero-stream timeout+retry?»* — YES: the stream idle watchdog (providerStreamIdleTimeout, 5 min) fired exactly as coded (the `attempt 2/3` replay in the log). The defect is the ARITHMETIC: 5-min idle window × up to 3 attempts > the 17-min task cap — the trial burns out without producing a token. The fix is bounding, not adding, the timeout.
- *«Reduce bench concurrency?»* — an option with a real cost (8→4 shards doubles wall time ~2h→4h). Cheaper first moves, in order: (a) bench-specific short idle timeout via the existing `providerTimeouts:` config seam (60–90s — fail-fast, 5+ attempts fit inside the same cap), (b) fallback take-over on zero-byte stall, (c) only if timeouts persist after (a)+(b) — cut shard concurrency or stagger shard starts. The shard-spread of the hangs (2/1/2/0/1/2, no start-peak concentration) does NOT prove subscription saturation, so concurrency is the last lever, not the first.

**Deeper log evidence (owner's race-condition question, 2026-10-06):** the hang is NOT only a cold-start. `chess-best-move` shows a WORKING agent (a `read` tool call answered with FileError) whose NEXT provider request then hangs zero-byte. Same spinner-only shape in `gpt2-codegolf`. Pattern: mid-conversation requests hang, not just the first one.

**Race-condition hypothesis to investigate (likely prime suspect):** the shared keep-alive provider HTTP client (sharedProviderHttpClient) reuses pooled connections; in bench containers (docker → NAT → internet), conntrack/NAT silently drops idle TCP, leaving HALF-OPEN sockets: a retry or a follow-up request written into a half-open pooled connection is accepted locally and never answered — zero bytes forever, until the 5-min idle watchdog aborts. It fits every observation: hangs mid-conversation (pool reuse after tool-call gaps), retries hanging identically (retry may pick the SAME poisoned pool entry), spread across shards (per-container NAT state), zero tokens.
**Consequences for the fix:**
- A watchdog replay MUST dial a FRESH connection (evict the pool entry / bypass keep-alive for the retry), not reuse the socket that just delivered zero bytes.
- Cheap validation: TCP keepalive or a shorter idle floor on the bench profile (providerTimeouts) would surface half-opens sooner; if hang count collapses with keep-alive DISABLED in a test bench run, the hypothesis is confirmed.
- Add to AC1: a fixture where the server accepts the socket and never replies must show the retry arriving on a NEW connection (assert connection reuse-off for watchdog replays).

**Field evidence — this hits INTERACTIVE users, not just bench (2026-10-06, second developer's report via owner):** in the fa TUI the same zero-byte hang shows as: you send a message, the agent «thinks», you come back an HOUR later to «agent stalled» with zero output — one overnight session sat «agent staled for 570 minutes». The session is effectively lost («сессия в сраку идёт»). The omp tool on the same machine/provider has NEVER done this to him («с тех пор ни одной такой проблемы»). So the class is user-facing and retention-critical, not a bench corner case.

**What this adds to the fix:**
- The TUI stall detector («agent stalled» notice) REPORTS but does not RECOVER — the turn hangs forever unless the user babysits. The bounded-replay + fallback fix must apply to the interactive path exactly as to bench: a wedged zero-byte request must surface as a retried/failed-over TURN, never a silent stall.
- AC addition: **AC4 — interactive recovery**: with the synthetic zero-byte fixture, a TUI session shows the retry/fallback happening in-band (and the turn completing or failing with a named error within the bounded budget) — «stalled for N minutes» as a terminal state is eliminated.
- Severity note for triage: user quote — he switched back to omp because of this; treat as P1.

## NEVER-AGAIN

- **NG1**: a synthetic provider fixture that accepts and streams nothing must produce: watchdog fires → bounded replays → error verdict with the zero-byte classification — covered by a unit test at the stream/watchdog layer (provider_common.dart).
- **NG2**: bench aggregate reports the zero-token-timeout count explicitly (regression guard for provider health across bench runs).

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: replay-into-hang no longer burns the whole cap: measured on the synthetic fixture, verdict time ≈ N×watchdog-interval, not the full agent cap.
- AC2: fallback take-over on zero-byte stall proven in a test (primary hangs, secondary answers, turn completes with the fallback's model recorded).
- AC3: bench summary split lands (NG2); the next full-dataset run shows the classification without log diving.

+        # (provider hang) next to one that burned real tokens before the
+        # cap, other failure modes untouched.

+"""gh-1308 NG2/AC3: the run summary separates zero-token provider hangs
+from real cap-exhausted timeouts, and reports the zero-token-timeout
+count explicitly — a regression guard for provider health across bench
+runs (today an `agent_timeout` row is indistinguishable from a trial
+that did real work until someone opens the agent logs).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
+"""
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
+    "summary_legacy", Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "summary.py"
+)
+summary = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+sys.modules["summary_legacy"] = summary
+spec.loader.exec_module(summary)
+
+
+def trial(task, name, resolved, mode, tin, tout):
+    return {
+        "task_id": task,
+        "trial_name": name,
+        "is_resolved": resolved,
+        "failure_mode": mode,
+        "total_input_tokens": tin,
+        "total_output_tokens": tout,
+    }
+
+
+class ZeroTokenTimeoutSplitTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.runs = Path(self.tmp.name)
+        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
+
+    def write_run(self, results):
+        run = self.runs / "shard-1"
+        run.mkdir(parents=True)
+        (run / "results.json").write_text(json.dumps({"results": results}))
+
+    def test_ng2_zero_token_timeouts_counted_explicitly(self):
+        # The gh-1308 evidence shape: agent_timeout rows with 0 tokens
+        # (provider hang) next to one that burned real tokens before the
+        # cap, other failure modes untouched.
+        self.write_run([
+            trial("t1", "x.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "agent_timeout", 0, 0),
+            trial("t2", "y.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "agent_timeout", None, None),
+            trial("t3", "z.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "agent_timeout", 4200, 900),
+            trial("t4", "w.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "tests_failed", 800, 200),
+            trial("t5", "v.1-of-1.shard-1", True, None, 120, 40),
+        ])
+        lines, problems = summary.render(self.runs)
+        out = "\n".join(lines)
+        self.assertEqual(problems, [])
+        # NG2: the explicit count — the provider-health regression guard.
+        self.assertIn("zero-token timeouts (provider hang): 2", out)
+        self.assertIn("1 with real work (cap exhausted)", out)
+        # AC3: the failure families carry the split, so the classification
+        # is visible without log diving.
+        self.assertIn("agent_timeout (0 tokens — provider hang) / no: 2", out)
+        self.assertIn("agent_timeout (real work, cap exhausted) / no: 1", out)
+        # A flat `agent_timeout` family row must NOT survive the split.
+        self.assertNotIn("- agent_timeout /", out)
+
+    def test_no_agent_timeout_rows_no_split_line(self):
+        self.write_run([
+            trial("t1", "x.1-of-1.shard-1", True, None, 10, 5),
+            trial("t2", "y.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "tests_failed", 0, 0),
+        ])
+        lines, _ = summary.render(self.runs)
+        out = "\n".join(lines)
+        self.assertNotIn("zero-token timeouts", out)
+        self.assertNotIn("provider hang", out)
+
+

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

            # One model per trial is the norm; mixed → None (cost n/a).
            "model": models[0] if len(models) == 1 else None,
            "estimated": usage.estimated_tokens,
        }
    return facts


def _cost_cell(pricing, facts, trial, tin, tout, model_override):
    """USD for one trial row; None renders n/a (unpriced/unknown model)."""
    model = (facts.get(trial) or {}).get("model") or model_override
    entry = fa_usage.price_entry(pricing, model) if model else None
    if entry is None:
        return None
    return fa_usage.cost_usd(entry, tin or 0, tout or 0)


def render(runs_dir: Path, expected=None, model_override=None):
    """Build the summary (lines, problems) for a runs dir — pure, testable."""
    runs_dir = Path(runs_dir)
    paths = sorted(glob.glob(str(runs_dir / "*" / "results.json")))
    lines = ["### fa on terminal-bench", ""]
    problems = []

    if not paths:
        lines.append("**No results.json produced — the tb run did not complete.**")
        problems.append("no results.json produced")
        return lines, problems

    pricing = fa_usage.load_pricing(_PRICING_PATH)
    facts = _session_facts(runs_dir)
    rows = []
    for p in paths:
        data = json.loads(Path(p).read_text())
        for r in data.get("results", []):
            resolved = r.get("is_resolved")
            mark = {True: "yes", False: "no", None: "pending"}[resolved]
            tin = r.get("total_input_tokens")
            tout = r.get("total_output_tokens")
            cost = _cost_cell(
                pricing, facts, r.get("trial_name", "?"), tin, tout, model_override
            )
            rows.append((
                r.get("task_id", "?"), r.get("trial_name", "?"), mark,
                r.get("failure_mode") or "", tin, tout, cost,
            ))
    n_resolved = sum(1 for r in rows if r[2] == "yes")
    accuracy = n_resolved / len(rows) if rows else 0.0
    missing = expected - len(rows) if expected is not None else 0
    note = (
        f" — {expected - len(rows)} of {expected} expected tasks missing"
        " (shard lost or timed out)" if expected is not None and len(rows) < expected else ""
    )
    lines.append(
        f"**{n_resolved}/{len(rows)} resolved — accuracy {accuracy:.0%}{note}**"
    )

    # Failure families (issue #142): the re-run delta is reported per
    # cluster, not just as one accuracy number. `unset` covers both
    # resolved trials (tb's default mode) and unresolved ones whose
    # tests ran and failed — the model side.
    #
    # gh-1308 (NG2/AC3): agent_timeout rows split by recorded tokens —
    # a 0-token timeout is a provider hang (the endpoint accepted the
    # request and streamed nothing), not a trial that ran out of clock
    # doing real work. The explicit count is the provider-health
    # regression guard across bench runs.
    modes = {}
    hang = work = 0
    for _, _, mark, mode, tin, tout, _ in rows:
        key = mode or "unset"
        if key == "agent_timeout":
            if not tin and not tout:
                key = "agent_timeout (0 tokens — provider hang)"
                hang += 1
            else:
                key = "agent_timeout (real work, cap exhausted)"
                work += 1
        modes[(key, mark)] = modes.get((key, mark), 0) + 1
    lines.append("Failure families (mode x resolved):")
    for (mode, mark), n in sorted(modes.items()):
        lines.append(f"- {mode or 'unset'} / {mark}: {n}")
    if hang or work:
        lines.append(
            f"**zero-token timeouts (provider hang): {hang}**"
            f" — agent_timeout split: {hang} with 0 tokens (provider hang),"
            f" {work} with real work (cap exhausted)"
        )
    lines.append("")

    # Token/cost totals (issue #1123): sums over exactly the rows above.
    total_in = sum(r[4] or 0 for r in rows)
    total_out = sum(r[5] or 0 for r in rows)
    priced = [r[6] for r in rows if r[6] is not None]
    # Same unpriced rule as the harbor summary: only rows that recorded
    # tokens but carry no price count. Zero-token rows render n/a but are
    # not unpriced spend.
    unpriced = sum(1 for r in rows if (r[4] or r[5]) and r[6] is None)
    if any(r[4] or r[5] for r in rows):
        cost_total = f"${sum(priced):.4f}" if priced else "n/a"
        suffix = f" — {unpriced} trial(s) unpriced (model missing from pricing.json)" if unpriced else ""
        lines.append(f"**tokens in/out: {total_in}/{total_out} — est. cost: {cost_total}{suffix}**")
        estimated = sum((facts.get(r[1]) or {}).get("estimated", 0) for r in rows)
        if estimated:
            lines.append(
                f"includes ~{estimated} estimated tokens (chars/4 where the provider omitted usage)"
            )
    lines.append("| task | trial | resolved | failure mode | tokens in/out | est cost |")
    lines.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for task, trial, mark, mode, tin, tout, cost in rows:
        tokens = f"{tin}/{tout}" if tin is not None or tout is not None else ""

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1311
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1311
- **Title**: gh-1308 [BUG] bench: GLM zero-byte hangs burn the whole agent cap — 11/59 trials died at 0 tokens (watchdog replays, cap clock keeps ticking, no fallback take-over)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1308` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +965
- **Deletions**: -334
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T09:11:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T12:13:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #1308
### Root Cause

- A GLM/zai endpoint that accepts requests but streams nothing was killed only by the agent's one-shot run-idle watchdog; the transient-retry ladder replayed the watchdog-cancelled request, but the watchdog timer was never re-armed — the replay ran unbounded until the trial cap, recording `agent_timeout` with 0 tokens (run 37418229569: 11/59 trials).
- The zero-byte replay class also never engaged the model-roles fallback chain: its verdict matched no transport pattern, so a hung primary was never handed off to the next configured model.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`: after 2 consecutive pre-commit attempts killed by the run-idle watchdog with zero output, the ladder stops replaying and fails the call with a retryable `zero-byte stall` terminal (`zeroByteStallTag`, `maxZeroByteWatchdogAttempts = 2`) instead of spending the remaining budget — verdict lands at ≈ 2×watchdog-interval, not the cap. Other failure classes keep the full 3-attempt budget.
- `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`: the run-idle watchdog re-arms after each fire while the run is active, so every replayed silent attempt is bounded by the same interval (a user abort that won the race is never revived).
- `lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart` + `providers_queue_runtime.dart`: the zero-byte verdict classifies as an immediate advance — the wedged primary is skipped, the next chain entry takes over (the 429 take-over path), no same-entry paid retries (each would cost another watchdog interval).
- `bench/terminal_bench/summary.py`: `agent_timeout` rows split into `agent_timeout (0 tokens — provider hang)` vs `agent_timeout (real work, cap exhausted)`, with an explicit `zero-token timeouts (provider hang): N` count (NG2).

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/transient_retry_stream_test.dart`: synthetic silent fixture — watchdog fires → bounded replays (2, was 3) → error verdict carrying the zero-byte classification, transport-classified (NG1/AC1).
- `test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_test.dart`: real-clock end-to-end — both silent attempts watchdog-killed, run ends as a retryable error at ≈ 2×interval, well under a minutes-long cap (AC1).
- `test/model_roles/fallback_stream_test.dart`: primary zero-byte stall → `modelFallback` notice → secondary answers, its model recorded (AC2); queue classifier: zero-byte verdict → timeout death, immediate.
- `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary.py` (new): the NG2 split and explicit count; non-timeout rows render unchanged.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — 9140 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures; bench python suites (terminal_bench + harbor_fa, 54 tests) green.

### Notes

- The generic 3-attempt transient budget, the connect-stall retry leg, and every non-watchdog failure class are byte-identical — only the zero-byte watchdog class is bounded.
- A sole (no-fallback) chain now fails truthfully after the zero-byte budget instead of hanging to the cap; users can raise `agent.runIdleTimeout` / `providerTimeouts:` for legitimately slow reasoning endpoints.

# gh-1308: [BUG] bench: GLM zero-byte hangs burn the whole agent cap — 11/59 trials died at 0 tokens (watchdog replays, cap clock keeps ticking, no fallback take-over)

## Description

**Evidence** (TBench full-dataset run [37418229569](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37418229569), 2026-10-06, glm-5.3-flash, 8 shards): 11 of the first 59 scored trials died as `agent_timeout` with **0 input / 0 output tokens** — while `unset`-failures in the same run recorded real usage (2–18k tokens), so accounting works and these trials genuinely never received a single token.

Root mechanism (from trial `polyglot-c-py` agent.log, cap 1020s):

```
fa -p 'Write me a single file in /app/main.c.py ...'
note: provider zai (zai) from FA_PROVIDER_* env
… reasoning 60s
… reasoning 120s
… (nothing but "reasoning" for 480s)
[net] connection lost (run-idle watchdog replay of zero-byte request: Request was aborted) — retrying in 5s (attempt 2/3)
… reasoning 540s … 1020s  → agent_timeout, 0 tokens
```

The GLM endpoint accepts the request and streams **zero bytes for 8+ minutes**; the run-idle watchdog correctly detects and replays (attempt 2/3), the replay ALSO returns zero bytes, and the cap clock keeps burning through every retry — trial dies having never started. 11 timeout trials, spread across shards (2/1/2/0/1/2 — not one bad runner): blind-maze-explorer-algorithm (2100s cap), git-multibranch, gpt2-codegolf, path-tracing, play-zork, polyglot-c-py, polyglot-rust-c, raman-fitting.easy, chess-best-move, write-compressor, sanitize-git-repo.hard. (play-zork/git-multibranch additionally show the stuck-call watchdog — secondary pattern: endless foreground commands; the zero-byte hang is the primary one.)

**Interpretation:** provider-side hang (zai/glm under 8-shard concurrency or on hard prompts with thinking), amplified by harness retry semantics: zero-byte replays restart reasoning from zero while the trial cap keeps ticking, and no fallback model is engaged (the 429 mid-turn take-over exists; zero-byte stall does not trigger it).

**Fix directions (choose per design):**
1. Zero-byte replays consume a bounded provider-time budget: after N (e.g. 2) consecutive zero-byte replays, the turn FAILS as a retryable error instead of burning the remaining cap — the trial dies fast and truthfully (error, not timeout).
2. Watchdog zero-byte stall triggers the model-roles fallback chain (same as 429 take-over) — a hung primary hands off to the next configured model instead of replaying into the same wedged endpoint.
3. Bench observability: the run summary should separate `agent_timeout (0 tokens — provider hang)` from `agent_timeout (real work, cap exhausted)` — today they are indistinguishable without opening logs.

**Owner questions, answered in the design (2026-10-06):**
- *«Isn't there already a zero-stream timeout+retry?»* — YES: the stream idle watchdog (providerStreamIdleTimeout, 5 min) fired exactly as coded (the `attempt 2/3` replay in the log). The defect is the ARITHMETIC: 5-min idle window × up to 3 attempts > the 17-min task cap — the trial burns out without producing a token. The fix is bounding, not adding, the timeout.
- *«Reduce bench concurrency?»* — an option with a real cost (8→4 shards doubles wall time ~2h→4h). Cheaper first moves, in order: (a) bench-specific short idle timeout via the existing `providerTimeouts:` config seam (60–90s — fail-fast, 5+ attempts fit inside the same cap), (b) fallback take-over on zero-byte stall, (c) only if timeouts persist after (a)+(b) — cut shard concurrency or stagger shard starts. The shard-spread of the hangs (2/1/2/0/1/2, no start-peak concentration) does NOT prove subscription saturation, so concurrency is the last lever, not the first.

**Deeper log evidence (owner's race-condition question, 2026-10-06):** the hang is NOT only a cold-start. `chess-best-move` shows a WORKING agent (a `read` tool call answered with FileError) whose NEXT provider request then hangs zero-byte. Same spinner-only shape in `gpt2-codegolf`. Pattern: mid-conversation requests hang, not just the first one.

**Race-condition hypothesis to investigate (likely prime suspect):** the shared keep-alive provider HTTP client (sharedProviderHttpClient) reuses pooled connections; in bench containers (docker → NAT → internet), conntrack/NAT silently drops idle TCP, leaving HALF-OPEN sockets: a retry or a follow-up request written into a half-open pooled connection is accepted locally and never answered — zero bytes forever, until the 5-min idle watchdog aborts. It fits every observation: hangs mid-conversation (pool reuse after tool-call gaps), retries hanging identically (retry may pick the SAME poisoned pool entry), spread across shards (per-container NAT state), zero tokens.
**Consequences for the fix:**
- A watchdog replay MUST dial a FRESH connection (evict the pool entry / bypass keep-alive for the retry), not reuse the socket that just delivered zero bytes.
- Cheap validation: TCP keepalive or a shorter idle floor on the bench profile (providerTimeouts) would surface half-opens sooner; if hang count collapses with keep-alive DISABLED in a test bench run, the hypothesis is confirmed.
- Add to AC1: a fixture where the server accepts the socket and never replies must show the retry arriving on a NEW connection (assert connection reuse-off for watchdog replays).

**Field evidence — this hits INTERACTIVE users, not just bench (2026-10-06, second developer's report via owner):** in the fa TUI the same zero-byte hang shows as: you send a message, the agent «thinks», you come back an HOUR later to «agent stalled» with zero output — one overnight session sat «agent staled for 570 minutes». The session is effectively lost («сессия в сраку идёт»). The omp tool on the same machine/provider has NEVER done this to him («с тех пор ни одной такой проблемы»). So the class is user-facing and retention-critical, not a bench corner case.

**What this adds to the fix:**
- The TUI stall detector («agent stalled» notice) REPORTS but does not RECOVER — the turn hangs forever unless the user babysits. The bounded-replay + fallback fix must apply to the interactive path exactly as to bench: a wedged zero-byte request must surface as a retried/failed-over TURN, never a silent stall.
- AC addition: **AC4 — interactive recovery**: with the synthetic zero-byte fixture, a TUI session shows the retry/fallback happening in-band (and the turn completing or failing with a named error within the bounded budget) — «stalled for N minutes» as a terminal state is eliminated.
- Severity note for triage: user quote — he switched back to omp because of this; treat as P1.

## NEVER-AGAIN

- **NG1**: a synthetic provider fixture that accepts and streams nothing must produce: watchdog fires → bounded replays → error verdict with the zero-byte classification — covered by a unit test at the stream/watchdog layer (provider_common.dart).
- **NG2**: bench aggregate reports the zero-token-timeout count explicitly (regression guard for provider health across bench runs).

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: replay-into-hang no longer burns the whole cap: measured on the synthetic fixture, verdict time ≈ N×watchdog-interval, not the full agent cap.
- AC2: fallback take-over on zero-byte stall proven in a test (primary hangs, secondary answers, turn completes with the fallback's model recorded).
- AC3: bench summary split lands (NG2); the next full-dataset run shows the classification without log diving.

Assigning ai-teammate per owner directive for this flow. Refs: #1122 (cap ladder), #1185 (liveness watchdog family), provider watchdogs in provider_common.dart; run 37418229569 artifacts tb-runs-shard-* (agent.log per trial).

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gh-1308 NG2/AC3: the run summary separates zero-token provider hangs
+from real cap-exhausted timeouts, and reports the zero-token-timeout
+count explicitly — a regression guard for provider health across bench
+runs (today an `agent_timeout` row is indistinguishable from a trial
+that did real work until someone opens the agent logs).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
+"""
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
+    "summary_legacy", Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "summary.py"
+)
+summary = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+sys.modules["summary_legacy"] = summary
+spec.loader.exec_module(summary)
+
+
+def trial(task, name, resolved, mode, tin, tout):
+    return {
+        "task_id": task,
+        "trial_name": name,
+        "is_resolved": resolved,
+        "failure_mode": mode,
+        "total_input_tokens": tin,
+        "total_output_tokens": tout,
+    }
+
+
+class ZeroTokenTimeoutSplitTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.runs = Path(self.tmp.name)
+        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
+
+    def write_run(self, results):
+        run = self.runs / "shard-1"
+        run.mkdir(parents=True)
+        (run / "results.json").write_text(json.dumps({"results": results}))
+
+    def test_ng2_zero_token_timeouts_counted_explicitly(self):
+        # The gh-1308 evidence shape: agent_timeout rows with 0 tokens
+        # (provider hang) next to one that burned real tokens before the
+        # cap, other failure modes untouched.
+        self.write_run([
+            trial("t1", "x.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "agent_timeout", 0, 0),
+            trial("t2", "y.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "agent_timeout", None, None),
+            trial("t3", "z.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "agent_timeout", 4200, 900),
+            trial("t4", "w.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "tests_failed", 800, 200),
+            trial("t5", "v.1-of-1.shard-1", True, None, 120, 40),
+        ])
+        lines, problems = summary.render(self.runs)
+        out = "\n".join(lines)
+        self.assertEqual(problems, [])
+        # NG2: the explicit count — the provider-health regression guard.
+        self.assertIn("zero-token timeouts (provider hang): 2", out)
+        self.assertIn("1 with real work (cap exhausted)", out)
+        # AC3: the failure families carry the split, so the classification
+        # is visible without log diving.
+        self.assertIn("agent_timeout (0 tokens — provider hang) / no: 2", out)
+        self.assertIn("agent_timeout (real work, cap exhausted) / no: 1", out)
+        # A flat `agent_timeout` family row must NOT survive the split.
+        self.assertNotIn("- agent_timeout /", out)
+
+    def test_no_agent_timeout_rows_no_split_line(self):
+        self.write_run([
+            trial("t1", "x.1-of-1.shard-1", True, None, 10, 5),
+            trial("t2", "y.1-of-1.shard-1", False, "tests_failed", 0, 0),
+        ])
+        lines, _ = summary.render(self.runs)
+        out = "\n".join(lines)
+        self.assertNotIn("zero-token timeouts", out)
+        self.assertNotIn("provider hang", out)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →

  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,

  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy

- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
